sticker_location: Under the sink on the grey disposal body. The grey tag near the bottom of the unit shows the model and serial number.

parts.label: wall switch
parts.where: On the wall near the sink, or sometimes inside the cupboard under the sink. It turns the disposal on and off.

parts.label: sink stopper
parts.where: The plug that sits in the sink drain opening on top of the sink.

parts.label: rubber flap in the sink drain
parts.where: Just inside the sink drain opening. You can lift its edges with a finger when the power is off.

parts.label: sink drain ring
parts.where: The metal ring you see flat in the bottom of the sink, around the drain opening.

parts.label: spinning plate inside the drain
parts.where: At the bottom inside the sink drain, below the rubber flap. You can see it with a torch, but never touch it with fingers.

parts.label: red reset button
parts.where: A small red button on the flat bottom of the grey unit under the sink.

parts.label: small jam wrench
parts.where: The small silver crank-shaped tool that came with the disposal. It is often kept under the sink.

parts.label: center hole on the bottom
parts.where: In the middle of the flat bottom of the grey unit under the sink, next to the red reset button.

parts.label: power plug
parts.where: At the end of the cord from the bottom of the unit, plugged into the outlet under the sink on models with a cord.

parts.label: side drain pipe
parts.where: The pipe coming out of the side of the grey unit under the sink, carrying water away to the wall.

parts.label: dishwasher hose connection
parts.where: A small short pipe near the top side of the grey unit under the sink, where the dishwasher hose joins if you have one.

parts.label: twist lock ring under the sink
parts.where: The ring at the very top of the grey unit, holding it up against the bottom of the sink.

parts.label: model label
parts.where: The grey tag near the bottom of the grey unit under the sink.

symptoms: It just hums and won't grind
It stopped while I was using it
It buzzes then goes quiet

plan.diagnosis: Something hard, like a bone, pit or spoon, is likely stuck inside and stopping the plate from turning. The unit shuts itself off to protect the motor, so clear the jam before turning it on again.
safety: Turn the wall switch off before you start.
Never put fingers or hands into the disposal.
Take the jam wrench out before turning the power back on.
Use tongs, never fingers, to pull anything out.

steps.instruction: Turn the wall switch off
details: Leave it off until the last step.
Also turn the water off.
steps.check: The switch is off and the unit is silent.

steps.instruction: Put jam wrench into bottom center hole
details: Find the hole in the middle of the flat bottom.
Push one end of the wrench firmly in.
steps.check: The wrench sits in the bottom hole and does not fall out.

steps.instruction: Rock jam wrench back and forth gently
details: Keep rocking until it turns one full turn.
It may feel stiff at first, then loosen.
steps.check: The wrench now turns all the way around.

steps.instruction: Pull jam wrench out again
details: Never leave it in when you turn power on.
steps.check: The wrench is out and in your hand.

steps.instruction: Pull stuck food out with tongs
details: Shine a torch down the drain to see it.
Grip the stuck piece and lift it out.
steps.check: You can see the stuck piece in the tongs.

steps.instruction: Press red reset button underneath
details: Wait 3 to 5 minutes first so it cools.
Press lightly until it clicks and stays in.
steps.check: The red button stays in, not popped out.

steps.instruction: Run cold water and test switch
details: Turn cold water on first, then the switch.
Let it run a few seconds after grinding stops.
steps.check: The unit spins freely and water drains away.

plan.aftercare: Feed food in slowly with cold water running, and keep spoons and bones out of the sink.

problems.title: Hums but won't spin

symptoms: Nothing happens when I flip the switch
It is completely dead and silent
It worked yesterday and now it won't start

plan.diagnosis: The built-in safety switch on the bottom has probably popped out, which cuts power when the unit jams or gets too hot. Pressing it back in after the unit cools often brings it back to life.
safety: Turn the wall switch off before pressing the reset button.
Never put fingers or hands into the disposal.
If the plug or cord looks damaged, do not touch it and call a pro.

steps.instruction: Turn the wall switch off
details: Leave it off while you check underneath.
steps.check: The switch is off.

steps.instruction: Push power plug firmly into outlet
details: Only on models with a plug under the sink.
If yours has no plug, skip this step.
steps.check: The plug is pushed all the way in.

steps.instruction: Wait five minutes for motor to cool
details: The safety switch will not stay in while hot.
steps.check: Five minutes have passed with the switch off.

steps.instruction: Press red reset button underneath
details: Find the small red button on the flat bottom.
Press lightly until it clicks and stays in.
If it pops out again, wait and try once more.
steps.check: The red button stays in, not popped out.

steps.instruction: Run cold water and test switch
details: Turn cold water on first, then the switch.
If still silent, check your home breaker box for a tripped switch.
steps.check: The unit hums or spins when the switch is on.

plan.aftercare: If it trips again, clear any jam first instead of pressing reset over and over.

problems.title: Totally silent

symptoms: There is a bad smell from the sink
The disposal stinks even when it's empty
It smells like old food around the drain

plan.diagnosis: Old food is likely stuck inside the unit and on the underside of the rubber flap. A warm water and baking soda wash, as the manual describes, usually clears the smell.
safety: Turn the wall switch off before wiping the flap.
Never put fingers deep into the disposal.
Do not use strong drain cleaners in the disposal.

steps.instruction: Turn the wall switch off
details: Keep it off while you wipe the flap.
steps.check: The switch is off.

steps.instruction: Wipe underside of rubber flap clean
details: Lift the flap edges gently with an old toothbrush.
Wipe away any dark, slimy food bits.
steps.target_part: rubber flap in the sink drain
steps.check: The underside of the flap looks clean, not slimy.

steps.instruction: Put sink stopper into drain
details: Push it down so it seals the opening.
steps.check: The stopper seals the drain opening.

steps.instruction: Fill sink halfway with warm water
details: Stir in 1/4 cup of baking soda.
Use warm water, not boiling water.
steps.check: The sink is half full of warm, cloudy water.

steps.instruction: Pull sink stopper out quickly
details: Stand back a little as water rushes down.
steps.check: Water is rushing down the drain.

steps.instruction: Turn wall switch on briefly
details: Turn it on as the water drains away.
This washes loose bits off the inside walls.
Turn it off again once water has gone.
steps.check: The unit runs and the water drains away cleanly.

plan.aftercare: Run cold water for a few seconds after every use, and grind citrus peel now and then to freshen it.

problems.title: Smells bad

symptoms: Water sits in the sink and won't go down
The sink drains really slowly
Water comes back up when it runs

plan.diagnosis: Ground-up food or grease may be built up inside the unit or just past it, slowing the water. Freeing the inside plate and flushing with cold water helps if it is a small blockage; if no water moves at all, the blockage is likely further down the pipe.
safety: Turn the wall switch off before you start.
Never put fingers or hands into the disposal.
Do not use caustic drain cleaner in the disposal.
Do not keep running the unit if water will not drain at all.

steps.instruction: Turn the wall switch off
details: Also turn the water off.
steps.check: The switch is off and the unit is silent.

steps.instruction: Put jam wrench into bottom center hole
details: Push one end firmly into the middle hole underneath.
steps.check: The wrench sits in the bottom hole.

steps.instruction: Rock jam wrench one full turn
details: Rock back and forth until it turns fully.
This frees food stuck on the inside plate.
steps.check: The wrench turns all the way around easily.

steps.instruction: Pull stuck food out with tongs
details: Take the wrench out first.
Shine a torch down the drain and lift bits out.
steps.check: No chunks of food are visible inside the drain.

steps.instruction: Run cold water and test switch
details: Turn cold water on first, then the switch.
Let water run a few seconds after grinding.
If water still will not move, turn it off and call a pro.
steps.check: Water flows down the drain without pooling.

plan.aftercare: Never pour grease down the drain, and always flush with cold water for a few seconds after grinding.

problems.title: Sink won't drain

symptoms: There is water dripping under the sink
The cupboard under the sink is wet
I see drips on the disposal

plan.diagnosis: Water can drip from where the unit meets the sink, from the side pipe joint, or from the bottom of the unit itself. Filling the sink and watching where the first drip appears, as in the manual leak test, shows which one it is without taking anything apart.
safety: Turn the wall switch off before reaching underneath.
Keep water away from the plug and cord.
If water drips from the bottom center of the unit, stop and call a pro.
Do not take pipes apart for this check.

steps.instruction: Turn the wall switch off
details: Put a bucket or bowl under the unit.
steps.check: The switch is off and a bucket is in place.

steps.instruction: Dry side drain pipe with towel
details: Also dry the outside of the grey unit.
Starting dry makes the first drip easy to spot.
steps.check: The pipe and unit feel dry to the touch.

steps.instruction: Put sink stopper into drain
details: Push it down so it seals the opening.
steps.check: The stopper seals the drain opening.

steps.instruction: Fill sink halfway with water
details: Use plain tap water, nothing added.
steps.check: The sink holds water without draining.

steps.instruction: Pull sink stopper out
details: Water will rush through the unit at once.
steps.check: Water is draining through the unit.

steps.instruction: Shine light and find drip start
details: Drip at the top ring or side pipe means a loose joint.
Drip from the bottom center means call a pro.
Note where the very first wet spot appears.
steps.check: You can point to where the first drip starts.

plan.aftercare: Check under the sink for drips once a month so a small leak is caught early.

problems.title: Leaking underneath

symptoms: It makes a loud rattling noise
It sounds like something is bouncing inside
It got noisy after something fell in the sink

plan.diagnosis: A spoon, bottle cap or other hard object has likely fallen in and is being thrown around inside. Turning it off and lifting the object out with tongs usually stops the noise.
safety: Turn the wall switch off straight away and leave it off.
Never put fingers or hands into the disposal.
Only use long tongs or pliers to reach inside.

steps.instruction: Turn the wall switch off
details: Do not run it again until you check inside.
steps.check: The switch is off and the noise has stopped.

steps.instruction: Shine light down sink drain ring
details: Look past the rubber flap for anything shiny.
A spoon or cap is often easy to spot.
steps.check: You can see inside the drain clearly.

steps.instruction: Pull loose object out with tongs
details: Grip it firmly and lift it straight up.
Check nothing else is left inside.
steps.check: The loose object is out and in your hand.

steps.instruction: Rock jam wrench back and forth
details: Put it in the bottom center hole first.
It should turn freely one full turn.
Take the wrench out again afterwards.
steps.check: The wrench turns freely all the way around.

steps.instruction: Run cold water and test switch
details: Turn cold water on first, then the switch.
Listen for a smooth hum with no rattling.
steps.check: The unit runs smoothly with no rattling sound.

plan.aftercare: Keep the stopper in the drain when you are not using the disposal so things cannot fall in.

problems.title: Loud rattling

symptoms: It still hums after clearing the jam and pressing reset
The wrench turns freely but it won't spin

plan.diagnosis: If the plate turns freely with the wrench and it still only hums, the motor is likely worn out. Disposals usually last 8 to 15 years, and replacing the whole unit is the normal fix.
replacement_parts: A new disposal the same horsepower as yours (on the label)
safety: Never put your hand in the disposal.
Keep the switch off until it's replaced.

steps.instruction: Turn the wall switch off
steps.check: The switch is off.

steps.instruction: Turn the plate with the wrench once more
details: If it turns freely all the way around, the jam is gone.
steps.check: The wrench turns all the way around.

steps.instruction: Find the model label on the bottom
details: Use a flashlight and take a photo.
steps.check: You have a photo of the label.

steps.instruction: Call a plumber, or buy the same size unit
details: Same brand and horsepower makes the swap easy.
Tell the plumber the reset button and jam wrench didn't help.

plan.aftercare: Run cold water before, during and after grinding.

symptoms: Still completely silent after pressing reset
No hum and no sound at all

plan.diagnosis: If the reset button didn't bring it back and it's completely silent, power isn't reaching it: a tripped breaker, a dead outlet or a bad wall switch. The breaker is safe to check; anything past that is an electrician's job.
safety: Don't open the wall switch or outlet; that's mains wiring.

steps.instruction: Check the breaker panel for a tripped switch
details: A tripped breaker sits in the middle. Push it fully off, then on.
steps.check: No breaker is tripped.

steps.instruction: Unplug it and test the outlet with a lamp
details: The outlet is in the cabinet under the sink.
If the lamp stays off, the outlet has no power.
steps.check: You know whether the outlet works.

steps.instruction: Plug back in and test with cold water running
steps.check: It runs, or it's still silent.

steps.instruction: Still silent? Call an electrician
details: Say the breaker is on and the reset button didn't help.
Don't open the switch or the outlet yourself.

plan.aftercare: Press the reset button only after the motor has cooled for 5 minutes.

problems.cause: a dead switch, outlet or wiring

sink stopper, set beside the drain
rubber flap in the sink drain
small jam wrench, shown inserted for use
power plug at the under-sink outlet
twist lock ring under the sink
